about: Research sheet for the Arkansas county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files. County officers come from the harvest in data/mining/harvest/ar-adva-cvso-directory-2026-11-23.json.
name: Arkansas
phones_sentence: County veterans service officer phones and days come from the Arkansas Department of Veterans Affairs’ county directory dated November 9, 2026. Most officers work part of the week, so call before you go.

Four counties with no phone tied to them show the department’s main number and say so.

aging.source_title: National Long-Term Care Ombudsman Resource Center: Arkansas residents’ rights brochure (2026), Contact Your Ombudsman
aging.source_scope: The eight Area Agencies on Aging by region, each with its counties and phones, as printed in the brochure’s Contact Your Ombudsman list (the local ombudsman programs are housed in these agencies); read in full. County names printed as “Woodfuff” and “Montogomery” are Woodruff and Montgomery. The brochure is undated; the file was posted in May 2026.
aging.description: The Area Agency on Aging for this county: help at home, meals, caregiver support, transportation and benefits counseling for older adults and caregivers. Military service is not required.
aging.next_step_extra: The phones shown are the ones the state’s ombudsman brochure prints for each agency; ask for aging services. Arkansas’s Choices in Living Resource Center, 866-801-3435, also helps with long-term services.

programs.name: Arkansas veterans: county veterans service officers for claims help
programs.organization: County veterans service officers; Arkansas Department of Veterans Affairs
programs.description: Free help with VA claims, pension and survivor benefits from county veterans service officers. The Arkansas Department of Veterans Affairs lists a county veterans service officer for each of the 75 counties; many work only certain days.
programs.next_step: Choose your county for its service officer’s phone and days. The Arkansas Department of Veterans Affairs is at 501-683-2382.
constraints: Call before you go; most county officers keep part-time hours, and several share one phone across counties.

programs.name: Choices in Living Resource Center (Arkansas aging and disability resource center)
programs.description: Arkansas’s Aging and Disability Resource Center: information about long-term services and supports for older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 866-801-3435, Monday to Friday 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

sources.title: Arkansas Department of Human Services: Choices in Living Resource Center
sources.scope: Phone 1-866-801-3435, 8:00 to 4:00 Monday to Friday, and the ADRC description; from the page’s own summary (metadata), not its body text.

programs.name: Medicare counseling (SHIP) for Arkansas
programs.description: Free, unbiased Medicare counseling from the State Health Insurance Assistance Program: plan choices, enrollment, costs and help paying for Medicare.
programs.next_step: Call 877-839-2675 or use the locator to reach Arkansas’s program. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

sources.title: SHIP Technical Assistance Center: find your local SHIP
sources.scope: National locator and phone 877-839-2675; search excerpt (carried from the starter edition, reviewed November 2, 2026).

programs.name: Arkansas Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: Arkansas Department of Human Services, Office of the State Long-Term Care Ombudsman
programs.description: Independent advocacy for residents of nursing homes and assisted living, through local ombudsmen at the Area Agencies on Aging.
programs.next_step: Choose your county for its local ombudsman, or call 501-682-1001, the number the state brochure prints for the program. To report abuse, neglect or exploitation of an adult, call the Adult Maltreatment Hotline, 800-482-8049. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

programs.name: Free legal help for Arkansas veterans and older adults
programs.description: Free civil legal help for people with low incomes, including housing, benefits and family matters. Legal Aid of Arkansas also runs a statewide fair housing helpline.
programs.next_step: Call the helpline, 800-952-9243 (1-800-9 LAW AID), Monday to Thursday 9 to 11 a.m. and 1 to 3 p.m., and Tuesday evenings 5:15 to 7:15, or apply online any time. Fair housing helpline: 870-338-9834.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income and case type; no criminal cases.
Legal Aid of Arkansas’s application lists 31 counties, so it may refer you to another program; the helpline will say which.

sources.title: Legal Aid of Arkansas: Apply for Legal Aid
sources.scope: Helpline, its hours, the fair housing helpline and the counties on the application; read in full.

programs.name: VA health care systems serving Arkansas
programs.description: Arkansas veterans are served mainly by VA Central Arkansas Health Care (John L. McClellan Memorial Veterans’ Hospital, 4300 West 7th Street, Little Rock; 501-257-1000, toll-free 800-224-8387, with clinics including Conway, El Dorado, Mena, Mountain Home, Pine Bluff, Russellville and Searcy) and the Veterans Health Care System of the Ozarks (1100 North College Avenue, Fayetteville; 479-443-4301, toll-free 800-691-8387).
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic; border counties may be closer to a system in a neighboring state. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veterans service officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 75 counties have a county veterans service officer route (71 with the officer’s own phone; four use the state department’s line), one of eight Area Agencies on Aging and a local long-term care ombudsman. Four independent living centers cover 25 counties.
coverage_note: County veterans service officers come from the Arkansas Department of Veterans Affairs’ county directory dated November 9, 2026. Area Agencies on Aging and local ombudsmen come from the state’s residents’ rights brochure; independent living centers from the ILRU national directory. Reviewed November 23, 2026. Contacts are not telephone-confirmed.
